title: When the Salt Falls Again
premise: Ansel Zhou, a royal food-taster whose body has become a ledger of poisons and half-remembered spells, has spent twenty years hiding their small magic in a city that outlawed it. When the border wards collapse on the night the stars go out, Ansel discovers the wards were fed by a covenant between the human realm and the salt-folk of the drowned coast — a covenant broken by the crown Ansel serves. To restore it before the moon completes its thirteenth turn, Ansel must gather the scattered found-family who once shared their exile: a disgraced ward-smith, a tide-priest's daughter, and the ghost of the taster who trained them. In the end, Ansel rewrites the covenant with their own poisoned blood as ink, extinguishing their personal magic forever but returning the stars — and finding that belonging was never something they had to buy.
about_author: Silas Villalobos is the pen name of a former line cook from a coastal town who claims to have tasted every storm that ever came ashore. They write fantasy about kitchens, borders, and the people who feed both.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Ansel Zhou. Ansel works the palace kitchens, tasting for poison while secretly selling charms in the night market, establishing their double life and quiet loneliness. When a dish tastes of starlight — impossible, since the stars went out an hour ago — Ansel realizes the old magic is leaking back into the world. Emotional beat: wary longing beneath routine.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. The border wards fall at midnight; the city's outlawed mages feel it like a tooth breaking. Ansel's mentor-figure, the ghost-taster Wren, manifests for the first time in years to warn them: the covenant is broken, and the moon will complete its thirteenth turn before the realms seal apart forever. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: What the Tide Kept
chapters.summary: POV Marisol, the tide-priest's daughter, now a smuggler running salt past the fallen wards. She finds Ansel half-drowned in her cargo hold and recognizes the charm-seller who once saved her brother. Reluctantly she agrees to guide them to the drowned coast. Emotional beat: grudging trust kindling between strangers with history.

chapters.title: The Ward-Smith's Hands
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. In a prison workhouse they find Odile Ferran, the ward-smith who built the border wards and was jailed when the crown blamed her for their failure. Her hands are ruined; she insists only the original covenant-stone can teach anyone to rebuild what she made. Emotional beat: guilt met with forgiveness neither believes they deserve.

chapters.title: A Kitchen of Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV Wren, the ghost-taster, remembering — through Ansel's senses — the night twenty years ago when the four of them fled the purge together and scattered. The chapter reveals the covenant was broken deliberately by the young queen's regent, who fed the wards lies instead of sacrifice. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Salt on Every Doorstep
chapters.summary: POV Marisol. The company travels the dead coast, where villages have forgotten their own names as the sea withdraws. Marisol confronts her mother's tide-priesthood and its complicity in the broken bargain, nearly abandoning the quest. Ansel's small charms, freely given, begin restoring memory door by door. Emotional beat: belonging tested against shame.

chapters.title: The Regent's Table
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. Captured and brought before the regent, Ansel is forced to taste a banquet laced with covenant-ash meant to bind the realms to the crown alone. Ansel survives by the immunity of twenty years — then turns the tables, revealing the regent's crime to the court via a charm hidden in the wine. Emotional beat: the servant outmaneuvering power.

chapters.title: Where the Stars Went
chapters.summary: POV Odile. The company reaches the covenant-stone beneath the drowned coast and learns the truth: the stars are not gone but held — the stone swallowed them as collateral when the oath failed. Restoring the covenant demands a willing sacrifice of all one's magic, and Ansel is the only one whose blood carries both realms. Emotional beat: terror and terrible clarity.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. As the moon completes its turn, the regent's forces and the rising sea converge on the stone. Wren spends her last remnant holding the circle; Odile reshapes the ward-work; Marisol calls the tide to stand witness. Ansel writes the new covenant in their own poisoned blood, giving up their magic as the stars pour back into the sky. Emotional beat: sacrifice crowned with wonder.

chapters.title: When the Salt Falls Again
chapters.summary: POV Ansel, months later. Magic-less but unregretful, Ansel runs a kitchen at the rebuilt border where travelers from both realms eat side by side; Marisol, Odile, and Wren's remembered recipes fill the tables. The salt falls again each evening like a blessing. Ansel finally understands that family was the covenant all along. Emotional beat: homecoming, quiet and earned.
